packet-01 - unverified image reading (blind; no identification seen in context)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview)

Observation: a single photograph of about 20 separate parchment fragments (strips and
rectangular pieces cut from one or more leaves, apparently reused as binding waste) laid
on a black ground in three rows, with an X-Rite colorchecker at lower left and a cm scale
at right. Each fragment carries a pencilled modern shelfmark note (looks like "Stams,
StA, Frg. ..." with a number), running vertically on most pieces.

Orientation: many of the fragments are photographed upside down relative to their
script (e.g. row 1 pieces 1, 4 and others show inverted letter forms); some are upright.
Some pieces show text running at right angles.

Script and decoration (observations): small Gothic textualis/semi-cursive book hand in
brown ink, single column on the pieces visible (column width not complete on any
piece); red rubric lines (e.g. row 1 piece 1 and row 1 piece 4 each have a rubricated
heading line, partially underlined/struck in red); red paraph marks and red strokes
over letters throughout. Several pieces (row 1 piece 2, row 1 piece 6, row 2 piece 4)
show a narrow column of short single-word entries, each preceded by a red paraph or
red stroke, which looks like a list or index (tentative interpretation: a table or
alphabetical list of words or headings), followed by a red heading and running prose.
Row 2 piece 5 has two such narrow word-list columns. Enlarged red initials appear at
lower left of row 3 piece 2 and red corner-bracket marks on several pieces.

Tentative interpretation: prose text with rubricated headings and paragraph marks, plus
list/table columns; I do not infer the work.

Limitations of the overview: at this reduction no word is reliably legible. I read the
native-resolution tiles that follow.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-002.jpg (tile: row 1 piece 1, with left edge of row 1 piece 2 at right)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Observation: the script on piece 1 is upside down in this image (inverted relative to
the photograph). I had no tool to rotate it, so all readings below were made by
mentally inverting the letter forms and are much less secure than readings of upright
